paragraphs: Ephraim the scribe, Resh Lakish’s student, reporting him, Bava Metzia 119a. Barukh takes King Shapur’s remark as disparagement for disagreeing. Heilprin quotes it as “Bring afrayin to Resh Lakish.” The checked Bavli instead names Rabbi Shimon. In Barukh’s interpretation, Ephraim’s name prompts “Give his ashes to Resh Lakish,” like Rav’s curse to Karna, “A horn in his eye.” Some say a Persian favor-expression; Yuchasin’s gloss: Persian praise for a pleasing statement. Arukh: from ben porat, may such wise men multiply. Arukh also: Persian for strength, may his power and might prosper.
